item.title: Accessible Documents: Small Changes, Better Access
item.description:
Jeff Toorongian, Amy Blake
Creating accessible documents is easier when accessibility is considered from the start. This 45-minute session will introduce practical strategies for creating documents that are structured and formatted with accessibility in mind. We’ll review several foundational practices, including the effective use of headings, lists, meaningful links, alternative text for images, tables, and color and contrast. Along the way, we’ll look at common accessibility barriers and discuss how they can be avoided

item.title: A Quasipolynomial Algorithm for $\ell_\infty$ Contractions
item.description:
Ashkan Soleymani, Gabriele Farina
We give an algorithm for computing an $\eps$-approximate fixed point of any $d$-dimensional nonexpansion with respect to the $\ell_\infty$ norm in time $\log(1/\eps)^{O(\log^2 d)}$. At its core, our method uses a boosting argument to geometrically shrink a search region. Among other consequences, our algorithm implies that simple stochastic games can be solved in quasipolynomial time.

item.description:

Parallel AI agents can produce useful local edits yet degrade a shared solution when their edits are combined. We model this coordination problem as discrete block optimization with an exactly evaluable objective and a known dependency graph. Independent sets certify compatible edits whose verified gains, measured against the same current solution, add exactly. item.title: Dual Effect and Certainty Equivalence Revisited for a Linear-Gaussian Dual Control Problem
item.description:
Ying Wang, Yue Ju, Håkan Hjalmarsson
This paper revisits the relation between dual effect and certainty equivalence (CE) through a scalar linear-Gaussian model. In dual control, the current input affects not only the immediate cost but also the information available for future decisions, and hence the future cost. Dynamic programming (DP) provides a natural framework for formulating dual control problems. item.title: Rigidity of the ball for Hartree-type energies and second shape derivative via a continuity argument
item.description:
Dario Mazzoleni, Riccardo Moraschi, Berardo Ruffini
We study the second shape derivative of an optimal design functional involving a nonlocal term in order to prove rigidity of the ball. Our approach relies on a continuity argument that relates the second variation to that of the corresponding local problem. The model serves as a prototype for a broader class of shape optimization problems to which the same strategy may be adapted.
